subject: Next-step: schedule 60–90m infra immersion + prep items
messages:
From: Kimberly Park <kimberly@redwood.com>
To: Ari Klein <ari@brightmetrics.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 16 Apr 2027 15:02:00 -0700
Subject: Next-step: schedule 60–90m infra immersion + prep items

Hi Ari — thanks again for a productive discovery call earlier today. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we keep momentum: 

- Goal for next session: 60–90 minute technical immersion with our ML/infra team to validate performance targets, integration points (VPC/KMS), and a mutual runbook for a PoC.
- What we need from you before the deep dive: list of attendees (roles), representative inference workload (typical prompt/sequence lengths, qps), and any compliance constraints (data residency, audit window).

Proposed windows (all PT):
- Week of Apr 26: Tue 4/27 09:00–10:30 or Wed 4/28 13:30–15:00
- Week of May 3: Thu 5/6 10:00–11:30

Please let us know which window works or suggest two alternatives and we’ll lock calendar invites. I attached a short mutual action plan (MAP_BrightMetrics_v1.pdf) and a tentative 90m agenda.

Prep notes for your team:
- Bring one engineer who owns L3 infra/networking and one ML lead who can speak to token distribution and latency/throughput expectations.
- If you have example payloads (sample prompts + avg sequence length), drop them into the Drive link and we’ll pre-run rough perf estimates.

If you prefer a shorter 60-minute session, we can focus the agenda to: architecture + perf targets + PoC checkpoints.

Thanks — Kim
Kimberly Park | Senior Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
Redwood Inference | kimberly@redwood.com | (415) 555-0189

Thanks Kim — great summary. We’re keen to move forward. 

We can do Wed 4/28 13:30–15:00 PT (that slot works best for our infra folks). Tentatively putting: Ari (CS leader), Nina Rao (ML lead), Jae Park <jae@brightmetrics.com> (Infra), and myself. I’ll confirm Jae’s role title in the next note.

Two quick asks from our side before the session: 
1) Can you share an example of the sort of perf metric dashboard you’ll walk through (latency percentiles + token cost split)?
2) We use AWS in us-west-2 — will your team need any access or just sample payloads is fine for the initial sizing?

Appreciate the MAP — I’ll review and add our internal milestones.

— Ari

Ari — thanks for locking 4/28. I’m confirming on our side: Marissa (Solutions Lead) and Ben (Performance Engineer) will attend alongside Kimberly. We’ll run the session as a hybrid working meeting — agenda draft below: 

Proposed 90m agenda (open to trimming to 60m):
1) 10m — Intros & scope alignment (success criteria: latency p50/p95 targets, cost per 1k tokens)
2) 20m — Current BrightMetrics workload walk-through (Nina/Jae) + sample prompts
3) 25m — Redwood serving architecture & suggested config (batching, quantization, autoscale profile)
4) 20m — Runbook for PoC: test cases, metrics, lead owners, timelines
5) 15m — Q&A and next steps / calendaring follow-ups

Prep requests (so we can make the meeting high-fidelity):
- A small set of representative prompts (5–10) with avg/max sequence lengths
- Expected sustained qps and any burst patterns (times of day)
- Any compliance/redaction constraints we should know about

Ben — do you want to run a quick preflight perf run if Ari can drop sample data in the Drive link?

If 4/28 13:30–15:00 PT holds, I’ll send the invite and include a Zoom + temporary VPC peering checklist in the calendar attachment.

Cheers,
Marissa
Marissa Cole | Solutions Lead, Redwood Inference
marissa_cole@redwood.com | (415) 555-0222
